main_text.p: [illegible, ~60 letters] Praedes autem dabant, vt nisi intra nouam Prytaneiam pecuniam numerassent, vel ij ipsi, vel fideiussores duplum in publicum praestarent: manebant autem ignominiosi donec soluissent: quod si, vt dixi, intra nonam Prytaneiam debitum non expunxissent, in vincula coniiciebantur, & duplum praestabant: neque iam integrum erat, fideiussores dupli offerre. Vlpianus ad Timocratea: [illegible, ~70 letters] Repraesentabant autem vectigalium redemptores, antequam vectigalia exigerent, pecuniae partem aliquam, quae [illegible, ~12 letters] dicitur, ceteram vero pecuniam numerabant intra nonam Prytaneiam, quod [illegible, ~12 letters] vocant. Suidas: [illegible, ~40 letters] Quod si intra nonam Prytaneiam in publicum non praestitissent quod reliquum erat pecuniae, in neruo, vt iam diximus, habebantur, & duplu, quod [illegible, ~10 letters] vocant, praestabant, ex hac Lege:
Τοὺς τὰ τέλη ὠνουμένους, εἰ μὴ καταλύσειν τὰ χρήματα ἕως τῆς σύνάτης ἀρυτθμείας, τὰ δίπλα καταλύσειν. Publicani reliquatores vectigalium ad nonam vsque Prytaneiam, duplum in publicum praestanto.

Meminit huius Legis Demosthenes in Timocratea: [illegible, ~60 letters] Exemplum habes in hac dica apud Demosthenem [illegible, ~10 letters]. ΕΓΚΛΗΜΑ. [illegible, ~50 letters] ΕΓΓΡΑΦΗΝΑΙ ΤΟ ΔΙΠΛΟΥΝ ΤΩι ΔΗΜΟΣΙΩι. Eorum, qui praedes & fideiussores erant, bona publicantur, ex hac Lege.
Τὼ οὐσίαι δημοσίαι εἰ, ὡς ἀν ἐξυποδιμύος [?] τὴν τῆς πόλεως, μὴ ἀποδῶ τὼ ἐνύλιν. Si praedes in publicum non praestiterint, bona eorum publicantor.
Legem laudat Demosthenes ἐν τῷ πρὸς Νικόστρατον. Καίτοι οἱ γε νόμοι κελεύουσι τὼ οὐσίαι δημοσίαι εἶ, ὡς ἀν ἐξυποδιμύος ἢ τῆς πόλεως, μὴ ἀποδῶ τ' ἐνύλιν.
Nescio an ad hos praedes spectet fragmentum, quod e Legibus Solonis legitur apud Lysiam ἐν ᾧ τῷ Θεομνήστου α. illud hic adscribemus.
ΕΠΕΓΓΥΑΙΝ Δ' ΕΠΙΟΡΚΗΣΑΝΤΑ Fideiubeto iuratus Apollinem . . .
ΤΟΝ ΑΠΟΛΛΩ, ΔΕΔΙΟΤΑ ΔΕ . . . fugerit sibi metuens litis causa.

page.notes: Greek passages are blurred in the scan; words I could not read letter by letter are marked illegible rather than guessed, and the accents and breathings in the Greek lines I did read are uncertain. The Latin in the right-hand italic columns is legible. A small printed mark stands before "Τοὺς" in the left column and was left out. The printed "publicantor" is copied as printed. The Latin text is mostly legible; the Latin inside the illegible Greek spans is not transcribed.
